Erfahrung im Microsoft\-Umfeld (D365 / Power Platform) sowie im Solution Design und in der Architektur entsprechender Lösungen
Fähigkeit, Anforderungen in strukturierte und nachhaltige Plattformlösungen zu überführen

Strukturierte, analytische und pragmatische Arbeitsweise
Bereitschaft, Lösungen bei Bedarf auch selbst umzusetzen
Idealerweise Grundkenntnisse in Low\-Code\-Automatisierung und Erweiterungen (z. B. Azure Functions)
Bewirb dich noch heute

Über uns
Mit unseren innovativen und effektiven pharmazeutischen Lösungen setzen wir bei Zur Rose alles daran, das Leben der Menschen positiv zu beeinflussen. Unser Team von 500 Mitarbeitenden mit Hauptsitz in Frauenfeld verfolgt das gemeinsame Ziel, die Zukunft des Gesundheitswesens zu verbessern.

Da Qualität, Komfort und Effektivität bei uns besonders grossgeschrieben werden, können Patientinnen und Patienten ihre Gesundheit einfach, und sicher selbst in die Hand nehmen. Unser Anspruch ist es, künftige Anforderungen im Gesundheitswesen zu prognostizieren.

Bei der Entwicklung unserer Lösungen und Arzneimittel setzen wir auf ein hohes Mass an Zuverlässigkeit und Effizienz und kümmern uns um die komplexen Themen, damit unsere Kundinnen und Kunden sich entspannt zurücklehnen können.
Die funktionsübergreifende Teamarbeit wird durch unsere Unternehmenskultur gefördert, sodass jedes Teammitglied gleichermassen geschätzt und darin bestärkt wird, sich am Entscheidungsprozess aktiv zu beteiligen. Offene Kommunikation und Empathie stehen bei uns an erster Stelle. Dabei versuchen wir stets, einen gemeinsamen Nenner zu finden und somit Kompromisse zu vermeiden.
Unsere Leidenschaft bei Zur Rose besteht darin, die Welt positiv zu beeinflussen. Teilst du dieselben Werte und möchtest auch du das Leben der Menschen verbessern? Dann würden wir uns freuen, dich als Teil unseres Teams zu begrüssen. jpid2fd11a0jm jit0728jm jiy26jm

We're looking for a Partner Solutions Architect to join Fivetran + dbt Labs and own the technical relationship with our ISV partner ecosystem.
This is a global, product-facing partner role rather than a regional field role. You will be the person who decides — with our product team — what we build with our ISV partners and in what order, and the person who explains the combined dbt + Fivetran product offering to that ecosystem.

The ISVs in scope span business intelligence, semantic and metrics consumption, catalog and metadata, governance, observability, activation, and the fast-growing set of AI and agent platforms building against our metadata and MCP surfaces.
Success in this role will require developing a defensible prioritization point of view, a coherent technical narrative, and a repeatable way to enable partner architects and sellers.
Internally, the role sits at the intersection of field engineering, product management, partnerships, and partner marketing. You will work with product managers across both product lines, with the partner development managers who own the commercial ISV relationships, and with regional Partner Solutions Architects who carry ISV motions into their geographies.
This is a full-time, remote-based position in California.

Own the prioritization of partner product priorities across the ISV ecosystem for the entire product suite, working in partnership with product management to translate ecosystem demand into a sequenced, defensible roadmap input.
build and maintain a single, current view of ISV integration state, gaps, and opportunities across the combined platform — ingestion, transformation, Fusion, the semantic layer, catalog and metadata, open table formats, and agent interfaces.
Own the capability and technical messaging of the combined dbt + Fivetran platform to the ISV ecosystem, including reference architectures, integration patterns, and the joint value narrative partners use with their own customers.
Serve as the primary technical counterpart to ISV partner solution architect teams, and partner product leaders, and run the technical cadence with our top ISV relationships.
Support and help shape workshops, webinars, hands-on labs, and partner marketing events that carry the technical narrative into the ecosystem at scale.
Equip ISV partner field teams with the demo narratives, architectures, and use cases they need to position the combined platform accurately.
Act as the structured feedback loop from the ISV ecosystem into product and engineering — surfacing integration gaps, friction points, competitive dynamics, and roadmap opportunities with evidence rather than anecdote.
Partner with regional Partner Solutions Architects and Partner Development Managers so global ISV strategy translates into regional field execution.
Build reusable collateral, playbooks, and enablement assets that let the broader partner solutions architecture team run ISV motions without you in the room.
Travel approximately 30% for partner planning sessions, technical workshops, executive meetings, and ecosystem events, including international travel.
What you'll need
5+ years in solutions architecture, sales engineering, partner engineering, technical product management, developer relations, or another customer-facing technical role in data and analytics.
Direct experience with ISV, technology partner, or product partnership motions — a track record of shaping what a partner built, not only how it was sold.
Demonstrated ability to influence a product roadmap you did not own: gathering requirements, building a prioritization case, and getting it accepted by product leadership.
Strong hands-on background in SQL, data modeling, and modern data platform architecture, with genuine technical credibility in front of partner engineers.
Fluency across the modern data stack — ingestion, transformation, orchestration, warehouses and lakehouses, open table formats, semantic layers, catalogs, BI, and the emerging agent and MCP layer — and the ability to explain how the pieces fit.
Excellent technical writing. A meaningful share of this role's output is documentation partners read without you present.
Strong presentation and facilitation skills for workshops, webinars, and large partner technical sessions.
Comfort operating globally, and across highly cross-functional internal environments.
Proven ability to drive outcomes in ambiguous, fast-moving situations with many stakeholders and no direct authority.
What will make you stand out
Experience at or with a data ISV in BI, catalog, governance, observability, activation, or AI tooling.
Hands-on experience with dbt and with Fivetran .
Experience with partner-facing APIs, SDKs, or integration certification programs.
Experience building a partner technical community — office hours, developer advocacy, or champion programs.
Background in product management or technical product marketing alongside a field engineering career.
Familiarity with cloud marketplace motions and co-sell programs.
Experience navigating partnerships where the partner is also a competitor in part of the stack.
A track record of building credibility quickly with partner engineers, partner product managers, and internal product teams.

How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles.

We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

As the Manager of Commercial Applied AI Architects at Anthropic, you will drive adoption of frontier AI across our mid-market and SMB customers by leading a team of technical architects who help companies build and deploy with the Claude API, Claude Code, the Agent SDK, and Claude for Enterprise.

The Solutions Architect, Data Governance serves as the lead technical and strategic advisor for enterprise data governance initiatives within client engagements. This role works directly with executive stakeholders, data leaders, business teams, security organizations, and technical delivery teams to design and implement governance programs that establish trust, visibility, accountability, and control across enterprise data estates.
This client-facing delivery role focuses on structured data governance, including metadata management, business glossary development, taxonomy design, data lineage, stewardship operating models, data quality frameworks, governance monitoring, and Microsoft Purview implementation. The Solutions Architect defines governance strategy, designs governance architectures, leads customer engagements, and provides oversight throughout delivery of the governance workstream.
This role also advises organizations on governance readiness for modern analytics and AI platforms, including Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, Azure Data Services, and Microsoft 365 Copilot. Role Description
Data Governance Strategy and Architecture
Act as the lead subject matter expert for enterprise data governance, Microsoft Purview, metadata management, taxonomy development, and governance operating model design.
Lead governance discovery workshops, maturity assessments, roadmap engagements, and executive strategy sessions.
Design enterprise governance frameworks including stewardship models, ownership structures, governance policies, business glossaries, taxonomy standards, and metadata management processes.
Microsoft Purview Governance Leadership
Architect and oversee implementation of Microsoft Purview Data Governance capabilities including Unified Catalog, Data Map, Data Estate Insights, data lineage, metadata management, and business glossary solutions.
Establish governance standards for structured data assets across Microsoft Fabric, Azure Data Services, Power BI, SQL Server, Snowflake, Azure Databricks, and related platforms.
Guide customers in developing sustainable governance processes, governance operating procedures, and stewardship responsibilities.
Customer Advisory and Governance Transformation
Serve as a trusted advisor to executive stakeholders, data leaders, governance councils, and technical teams.
Translate business objectives, regulatory considerations, and operational requirements into scalable governance solutions.
Lead customer-facing workshops, architecture reviews, roadmap discussions, and governance design sessions.
Governance Operations and Monitoring
Design governance monitoring and operational reporting solutions utilizing Azure Monitor, Azure Log Analytics, and related observability platforms.
Establish operational processes for governance measurement, stewardship accountability, data quality reporting, lineage monitoring, and governance adoption tracking.
Contribute governance accelerators, reference architectures, and reusable delivery assets from engagement experience.
Apply the practice's delivery standards and AI-accelerated delivery patterns on engagements and identify opportunities for improvement based on real-world client conditions.
AI Readiness
Advise organizations on governance readiness for Microsoft 365 Copilot and enterprise AI initiatives.
Assess metadata maturity, lineage coverage, ownership models, and governance controls required to support effective and responsible AI adoption.
Behaviors and Competencies
This role is expected to demonstrate expert-level capability within data governance and strong capability across the following areas:
Subject Matter Expertise: Recognized depth in enterprise data governance, with sufficient understanding of data platforms to evaluate governance implications and identify risks in adjacent workstreams.
Facilitation: Leads discovery, maturity assessment, and governance design sessions to resolution, including situations involving disagreement over ownership or governance scope.
Communication: Explains governance concepts, trade-offs, and obligations to executive sponsors, business stewards, and technical teams while tailoring communication to the audience.
Relationship Management: Builds trust with executive sponsors, governance councils, and data stewards and sustains relationships through long-term governance initiatives.
Collaboration: Works across delivery teams, security organizations, and business units, measuring success by governance adoption rather than artifact delivery.
Problem Solving: Identifies and resolves root causes that hinder governance initiatives, including unclear ownership, ineffective incentives, or inadequate tooling.

We are looking for candidates who demonstrate strength across these areas. Deep expertise in every technology listed is not expected. Candidates should not self-select out if they do not meet every qualification.

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale.

More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box.

Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency.

Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.
Company Operating Rhythm
At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.
Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.
Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.
The Opportunity
Deepgram is investing in Arabic-language capabilities, and the customers who are building on them deserve a technical partner who speaks the language and knows the region firsthand. We are hiring an Applied Engineer to be that partner: the first member of our Applied Engineering team who is dedicated to Arabic-speaking markets. We would love for you to be based in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), and the search is open across the broader EMEA region.
You'll operate in the Solutions Architect role, leading the technical design and delivery of customer implementations across MENA, from kickoff through production cutover.

Because you'll be the first dedicated technical presence in the region, you'll also take a strong share of pre-sales work, including the technical discovery, proof-of-concepts, and evaluations that earn the technical win for regional prospects.

You'll represent Deepgram in front of customers and at regional events, and you'll bring what you learn back to our Product and Research teams, including how our Arabic models perform across dialects in production.
The region's time zones overlap fully with EMEA business hours, so you'll work alongside our EMEA Applied Engineers every day, and you'll help to extend coverage toward APAC hours as the team grows.
About the Solutions Architect Role at Deepgram
Solutions Architects at Deepgram own the periods when a customer's environment is changing (a new onboarding, a scaling deployment, a migration, a feature rollout). The work is hands-on and technical.

You'll design solutions that fit each customer's stack and constraints, drive the deployment work itself, and turn what each engagement teaches you into reusable patterns that compress how long it takes the next customer to reach value. In this seat, the motion extends into pre-sales.

For many regional prospects, you'll be the first Deepgram engineer that they meet, and the same skills that make implementations succeed (listening well, designing to constraints, showing working software) also win evaluations.
You'll be hired into the Applied Engineer position on our Applied Engineering team, which combines what other companies split into Sales Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Implementation, Forward-Deployed Engineering, and Technical Support, with a single growth ladder from Associate through Principal. The region is your focus; Applied Engineering is where you grow.

Own the technical design and delivery of customer implementations across MENA, from kickoff through production cutover
Lead technical discovery, proof-of-concept design, and evaluations for regional prospects, partnering with Account Executives through the sales cycle
Design solutions that fit each customer's stack, constraints, and data-residency requirements
Represent Deepgram in front of Arabic-speaking customers and at regional events
Bring the voice of Arabic-language customers to our Product and Research teams, including feedback on Arabic model performance across dialects
Develop reusable implementation patterns, reference architectures, and deployment playbooks that the broader team and customers can reuse
Provide support for the most complex post-onboarding cases in the region, and help to grow our coverage into APAC hours over time
Time Allocation
40% — Customer implementation and scaling engagements
25% — Pre-sales technical work, including discovery, demos, proof-of-concepts, and evaluations
15% — Building reusable patterns, reference architectures, and automation
10% — Documentation, knowledge sharing, and product feedback
10% — Complex post-onboarding escalations for regional customers
Your First 90 Days
First 30 Days — Complete comprehensive onboarding to understand Deepgram's technology, products, and competitive landscape. Gain proficiency with our core APIs and documentation. Shadow active implementation engagements and discovery calls across EMEA accounts to learn how the Applied Engineering team operates.
60 Days — Begin owning customer implementation engagements end to end, and lead technical discovery for regional prospects alongside Account Executives. Start contributing to reusable implementation patterns, and deliver your first Arabic-focused demo or evaluation asset.
90 Days — Own the technical relationship with your assigned regional accounts. Run evaluations and implementations concurrently, and establish a working feedback loop with our Product and Research teams on Arabic model performance.
You'll Love This Role If You
Want to be the first dedicated technical presence for a region and build the playbook that others follow
Enjoy the mix of customer conversations and hands-on building
Are passionate about bringing Voice AI to Arabic-speaking markets
Find satisfaction in designing patterns that scale beyond a single customer engagement
Communicate clearly with executives and in technical depth with engineers
Are energized by deploying cutting-edge Voice AI in production environments
It's Important To Us That You Have
Native or professional-level fluency in Arabic, and excellent written and spoken English
A base in the MENA region (preferred) or elsewhere in EMEA, in a country where our employment partner supports hiring

We’re looking for a Principal Architect to lead the design and delivery of complex, multi-domain systems spanning cloud, data, and AI. This role is ideal for a deeply experienced engineer who owns the hardest architectural challenges, sets technical direction, and serves as the senior technical voice on the engagements they support.
In this role, you will operate as the senior technical authority on a cross-functional team, defining architecture across cloud infrastructure, data platforms, and AI/ML workloads. You’ll partner closely with leadership and clients on technical strategy, mentor experienced engineers, and own high-stakes decisions that shape the long-term success of the systems you build.
Why This Role Matters
At Robots & Pencils, we design AI systems for a human world. Our name says it all. Robots and pencils means engineering paired with creativity, because every agent we ship has to work for real people in real workflows. That balance is baked into how we operate.
Every role here contributes directly to that mission. Here, you shape how AI systems integrate into enterprise operations, how teams move at real velocity, and how products create measurable impact for clients and the people they serve. We ship production-ready AI in 30 to 45 days. That pace demands people who take ownership, lead with craft, and care deeply about what they put their name on.

Craft & Delivery
Define technical strategy and lead architectural design across cloud, data, and AI/ML systems for end-to-end engagements
Architect scalable cloud-native solutions, including multi-cloud and hybrid strategies (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes)
Design data architectures including warehouses, data lakes, and pipelines for batch and streaming workloads (e.g., Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery, Spark, Kafka)
Design AI/ML systems including model serving, MLOps pipelines, feature stores, and LLM-based applications (e.g., SageMaker, Vertex AI, MLflow, Hugging Face)
Define infrastructure as code, CI/CD, and DevOps standards across engagements (e.g., Terraform, CloudFormation, GitHub Actions)
Drive performance, scalability, cost, and reliability optimization across deployed systems
Ensure architecture meets security, governance, and compliance requirements (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA, SOC2)
Lead cloud migrations and platform modernization initiatives
Bring an AI-forward mindset to your daily work, using tools like Claude, Cursor, and other modern AI assistants to ship higher-quality work at pace
Collaboration & Communication
Partner with senior leadership and clients as the principal technical voice on strategy and direction
Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to engineering and non-engineering stakeholders alike
Engage closely with engineering, data, AI, and product teams to align architecture with broader business priorities
Develop and maintain architecture documentation, standards, and guidelines
Leadership & Influence
Define and champion architectural standards and best practices on the engagements you support
Mentor experienced engineers and architects, helping them grow their technical judgment and impact
Own the most difficult architectural and integration challenges, serving as the senior technical decision-maker
Evaluate emerging technologies and recommend tools, frameworks, and patterns that improve architecture over time

8+ years of experience in software engineering, with at least 5 years in technical leadership roles
Deep expertise in cloud platforms and cloud-native architectures (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP)
Strong background in microservices, serverless, containers, and event-driven systems (e.g., Kubernetes, Docker, Lambda, EventBridge)
Proficiency with infrastructure as code and CI/CD (e.g., Terraform, CloudFormation, Pulumi, GitHub Actions)
Strong data architecture expertise across relational, NoSQL, and big data systems (e.g., PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, Spark, Kafka)
Hands-on experience with data modeling, ETL/ELT pipelines, and orchestration (e.g., Airflow, Prefect, dbt)
Strong experience designing AI/ML systems for production, including LLMs, MLOps, and model serving (e.g., SageMaker, Vertex AI, MLflow, Hugging Face, PyTorch, TensorFlow)
Solid understanding of networking, security, identity, and access management in cloud environments
Experience with governance, compliance, and observability frameworks
Strong software engineering skills (Python, APIs, containerization)
Track record of senior technical leadership and mentoring experienced engineers
Strong stakeholder communication skills, with the ability to translate technical depth across audiences
Demonstrable usage of AI-forward tools such as Claude and Cursor
Multi-cloud architecture experience, AI ethics or responsible AI experience, or enterprise architecture certifications (e.g., TOGAF, AWS/Azure/GCP) is a plus
Helpful Extras and Unique Skills
Experience designing AI/ML solutions that integrate with SAP EAM data structures (e.g., Equipment Masters, Work Orders, or Notifications) via SAP BTP or cloud-native APIs.
You’ll Do Well Here if You Are
A doer. You see something broken and fix it. You'd rather move on clarity than wait for certainty.
A fast learner who knows you don't know everything. The AI landscape changes weekly. You're senior enough to know better and curious enough to keep learning anyway.
Direct in a way that makes the work better. You give honest feedback. You'd rather have the hard conversation than blow smoke.
Obsessed with craft. You know genius is in the details. You ship exceptional, not perfect, and you don't put your name on work you wouldn't stand behind.
Built for ownership. You honor commitments, admit mistakes fast, and back your teammates when a decision costs something. No handoffs, no finger-pointing.
All in. You treat clients' businesses like your own. You take the work seriously without taking yourself seriously.
Resourceful when the budget, timeline, or team is tight. Constraints don't slow you down. They sharpen you.
Glad to be in the room with people who care as much as you do. Our teams average fifteen-plus years of experience. We hire people who push each other to do better work.

unsere Prozesse und Produkte kontinuierlich mit KI weiterzuentwickeln – erwarten wir von allen Berater:innen.

The infrastructure powering the AI era doesn’t sell itself, and the customers building on it don’t want to be sold to. They want a peer. You’ll work as part of a focused three-person team alongside one Account Executive and one Account Manager, together responsible for landing new accounts and expanding within them across the region.

The customers you’ll work with are AI labs, research institutions, and enterprises running some of the most demanding GPU workloads in the world.

This is a role for someone who shows up with substance, who can hold a real conversation about model training and MLOps tooling in the morning and cluster networking in the afternoon, and who finds the space between infrastructure and application more interesting than either on its own.

As an Account Solution Architect covering Northern EMEA, you’ll move across the full stack depending on what the customer needs, from ML training workflows and MLOps platforms like Weights & Biases to bare metal GPU infrastructure and physical AI deployments.

This isn’t a role built around a single layer of the stack, but the majority of your conversations will live in the ML layer. You’ll be expected to go deeper than most when the infrastructure conversation demands it, while staying commercially aware enough to support both new logo pursuits and in-flight account expansion.

This role requires up to 40% travel.

Cover Northern EMEA, with a focus on the Nordics and Benelux regions (Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland, Netherlands, Belgium, and Luxembourg).

As an Enterprise Solutions Architect at ClickHouse, you'll own the technical side of the sales cycle for enterprise accounts. You'll engage with data platform engineers, architects, SRE, and the VP who owns the standard — and your job is to design something that satisfies all of them and then prove it at production scale.
Getting an enterprise team there usually means moving them off something else, so most of your work is making that migration credible: the architecture, benchmarks run against their own data, and a plan their engineers believe they can execute.
This is a role for engineers who want the hard version of the problem: real scale, real constraints, and an incumbent to displace. Prior pre-sales experience helps but isn't required — technical depth is non-negotiable.
What You Will Be Doing
Own the technical evaluation for enterprise accounts — from discovery through POC or competitive bake-off, architecture sign-off, security review, and first production workload.
Engage across a wider set of stakeholders than a single team: data platform engineers, architects, SRE, security, and the executive who owns the standard. Design solutions that hold up with all of them in the room.
Design for production scale — sizing, sharding and replication strategy, ingestion topology, tiered storage, cost modeling, and what happens when something fails at 3am.
Win competitive displacements against Elasticsearch, Splunk, Snowflake, BigQuery, Druid, Pinot, and homegrown systems, using benchmarks the customer's own team can reproduce.
Own the migration plan — sequencing, dual-run, validation, and cutover — so the customer's team can see exactly how they get to production.
Clear the security and procurement path: questionnaires, compliance artifacts, network and identity architecture, and BYOC or private deployment requirements.
Partner closely with Enterprise AEs to progress and close opportunities — you own the technical win, they own the commercial close. Build the TCO case against the incumbent/competition together.
Advocate for customer needs internally with Product and Engineering — you're the voice of the technical buyer inside ClickHouse.
Contribute reference architectures, benchmark harnesses, migration guides, and objection handling material that help the team scale what's working.

Deep technical foundation in data infrastructure — built through experience as a data engineer, platform engineer, software engineer, DBA, or solutions architect.
Production experience with analytical databases (ClickHouse, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Druid, Pinot, Vertica) and with operating them, not just querying them.
Distributed systems judgment: partitioning, replication, consistency trade-offs, query execution, and a felt sense for where things break under load.
Fluency across the modern data stack — Kafka and CDC pipelines, orchestration, object storage, BI tools, and at least one major cloud (AWS, GCP, Azure) at architecture level.
Experience running a technical evaluation against a named competitor and winning it, including designing the migration off the incumbent and the parts of it that are genuinely hard.
Customer-facing experience with real stakes — pre-sales, consulting, technical account management, or a staff-level engineering role that put you in front of customers.
Strong written and verbal communication. You can whiteboard with a staff engineer in the morning and present to a VP of Engineering in the afternoon.
Comfort with longer cycles and more stakeholders. Enterprise evaluations don't close in three weeks, and you know how to keep one moving without letting it stall.
Willingness to say ClickHouse isn't the right tool for a given workload when that's true.

OpenAI Consumer Devices is building the next generation of products that bring powerful AI into people’s everyday lives. Guided by OpenAI’s mission to ensure AGI benefits all of humanity, our team combines world-class researchers, engineers, designers, and operators who care deeply about creating useful, intuitive, and responsible technology.

You’ll have the opportunity to work alongside exceptional people on ambitious, zero-to-one challenges at the intersection of hardware, software, and AI. This is a chance to help define an entirely new category of products—and shape how people experience AI in the future.
The Operating Systems team is critical in this mission, turning sophisticated hardware and AI capabilities into a reliable, trusted platform. Security is central to that work: we define trust boundaries, integrate hardware-backed protections, isolate sensitive context, and establish the guardrails that let AI applications and agents act safely, privately, and under user control.

We’re looking for a Software Security Architect to define the security architecture for OpenAI’s next-generation operating system. You’ll work alongside hardware security architects and partner with operating system, silicon, firmware, privacy, and product teams to protect users, their devices, and their data.
This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who can connect operating system internals, hardware-backed security, and real-world product constraints. Your work will shape the platform’s trust model, protect sensitive information, and set the technical foundations for AI that is safe, private, and under user control.

Define the operating system’s security architecture, trust boundaries, privilege model, and protections for sensitive user data.
Partner with hardware security architects to integrate roots of trust, secure elements, trusted execution environments, and processor security capabilities into the operating system.
Design foundational platform defenses, including secure boot, code signing, attestation, secure updates, key protection, and device recovery.
Establish isolation and access controls across the kernel, applications, system services, and AI workloads.
Define guardrails for how AI applications and agents access information, use sensors and tools, retain context, and act on a user’s behalf.
Lead threat modeling and architecture reviews across the platform, translating emerging threats into practical, enforceable requirements.
Prototype solutions, review security-critical systems code, and guide engineering teams through complex technical and product tradeoffs.

Deep experience designing or securing operating systems, kernels, embedded platforms, hypervisors, or other privileged systems software.
Complex understanding of operating system internals, including memory protection, process isolation, executable loading, device drivers, and privilege boundaries.
Experience building security architectures that span hardware, firmware, operating systems, applications, and cloud services.

Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation.

We are looking for an AI Agent Security Architect to function as the primary technical
authority for Replit’s autonomous and AI agent security blueprint. In this critical role, you
will design, implement, and maintain the runtime defense systems, guardrail
frameworks, and sandboxing architectures that govern AI agents executing code,
invoking tools, and reasoning across our platform. You will be a key technical
contributor—leading high-impact AI security initiatives and bridging the gap between
non-deterministic AI behavior and rigorous cybersecurity controls for both engineering
and executive leadership.

AI Agent Security Strategy & Technical Execution
AI Agent Security Blueprint: Define the long-term vision and architectural patterns for securing autonomous agent workflows, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, multi-turn reasoning loops, and multi-agent coordination.
Runtime Guardrails & Policy Enforcement: Architect and deploy dynamic input/output guardrail systems, semantic firewalls, and real-time intent verification filters to prevent goal hijacking, system prompt leaks, and indirect prompt injections.
Agent Execution & Tool Sandboxing: Partner with Infrastructure and AppSec teams to design secure, short-lived, micro-isolated environments (e.g., microVMs, WebAssembly, container sandboxes) where agents can dynamically execute code, run shell commands, and interact with host operating systems safely.
Agentic Threat Modeling & Red Teaming: Conduct specialized threat modeling against non-deterministic systems. Lead automated and manual AI red-teaming initiatives to uncover vulnerabilities in RAG context pipelines, vector stores, and tool-calling interfaces.
Identity, Delegation & Least Privilege: Architect fine-grained permission models and step-up Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) authorization patterns for agents acting on behalf of users—ensuring agents never exceed the delegated privileges of the end user or misuse API keys.
Context & Memory Boundary Security: Design strict data isolation and poisoning prevention controls for vector databases, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, and long-term conversation memories across multi-tenant workloads.
Risk Management & Cross-Functional Enablement
Maintain the AI Security Source of Truth: Define, document, and maintain authoritative secure design patterns and SDKs for engineering teams building internal or customer-facing AI agent capabilities.
Contribution to Risk Register: Identify, quantify, and document non-deterministic and agentic security risks (e.g., OWASP Top 10 for LLMs & AI Agents, MITRE ATLAS), ensuring they are accurately represented in the Cybersecurity Risk Register.
Auditability & Observability: Design tamper-evident logging and telemetry standards for agent reasoning chains, tool execution history, and context assembly to support incident response, forensics, and GRC requirements.
Compliance & Sales Enablement: Partner with GRC to translate complex AI security controls into enterprise-ready audit documentation (e.g., ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act readiness) and support Sales on complex enterprise security inquiries regarding AI safety.

6+ years of experience in security engineering or security architecture, with at least 2+ years dedicated specifically to AI/ML security, LLM application security, or securing agentic frameworks.
Deep understanding of agentic architectures and protocols (e.g., Model Context. Protocol (MCP), LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, ReAct frameworks, and vector database technologies).
Hands-on expertise with threat vectors unique to agentic AI: Indirect Prompt
Injection, Goal Hijacking, Tool Parameter Tampering, Data Poisoning, and Context Contamination.
Strong background in applying safety standards and risk frameworks such as OWASP Top 10 for LLMs & AI Agents, NIST AI RMF, and MITRE ATLAS.
Proficiency in Python, Go, or TypeScript/JavaScript with a proven track record of reviewing code and building functional security tooling or guardrails.
Experience authoring, maintaining, and evangelizing technical security architecture documentation.

The Pre-Sales Solutions Architect (SA) Leader owns the health, direction, and performance of the Solutions Architecture function. Where an individual SA is the technical owner within the sales cycle for their assigned opportunities, the SA Leader is accountable for technical win rate and deal velocity across the entire pre-sales motion — every channel the team supports, and the people who deliver against it.
The SA Leader is a player-coach: they carry direct accountability for channel coverage, the most strategic or highest-stakes evaluations, and cross-functional GTM alignment, while spending the majority of their time developing individual SAs so the team's proactive, commercially-sharp approach scales without becoming order-taking.
Compensation Note: SA Leader compensation is tied to team-wide ARR bookings — new logo, expansion, and multi-year commitments across every SA's pipeline, not just deals the Leader personally works. The Leader is expected to operate with the same commercial mindset as the team, at portfolio scale.

People Leadership & Team Development
The SA Leader hires, coaches, and grows the SA team so each member operates as a credible, commercially sharp technical partner in the sales cycle. This includes:
Hiring and onboarding new SAs, including calibrating them against the channel-specific technical evaluation prompts
Running regular 1:1s, reviewing deal strategy, PoC scoping, and objection handling, and giving direct feedback
Building and maintaining repeatable playbooks (discovery frameworks, PoC templates, objection/RFP responses, competitive positioning) so quality doesn't depend on tenure
Setting and holding the team to a consistent bar for technical depth, commercial instinct, and quota attainment
Channel & Coverage Ownership
The SA Leader owns the coverage model for the entire function — deciding, tracking, and rebalancing which SAs support which channels, and closing gaps as pipeline shifts. This includes accountability across all five channels in the SA Channel Mapping :
Direct Sales (AMER, EMEA, APJ)
Hyperscalers (AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI)
Accelerators, Incubators, VCs (YCombinator, TechStars, 500 Startups)
SfP + OAuth Partners (Lovable, Bolt, Anthropic)
Solution Providers ( Postgres.ai , Stormatics)
Rebalancing SA assignment across channels as pipeline volume, deal complexity, or new partner motions shift
Resolving coverage gaps (a channel with no dedicated SA depth, or a region outgrowing its current allocation) and deciding when a hire, a cross-channel reassignment, or a controlled exception is the right fix
Approving which opportunities warrant Leader-level involvement directly, versus staying with the assigned SA
Technical Sales Ownership (oversight)
The SA Leader ensures every significant opportunity has a clear, accountable technical owner across architecture fit, use cases, evaluation criteria, and competitive positioning — spot-checking deal documentation and risk tracking across the pipeline, and stepping in directly on the largest or most strategic evaluations.

The SA Leader ensures the team consistently qualifies opportunities as technically winnable early, coaching SAs on discovery quality and holding the team accountable for surfacing deal-level risk to AEs and sales leadership before it costs a deal.
Proof of Concept and Evaluation Support (oversight)
The SA Leader ensures PoCs across the team are scoped to demonstrate differentiated value, not just technical box-checking — auditing success criteria, evaluation structure, and win-rate patterns across the whole book of active evaluations.
Technical Objection Handling (oversight)
The SA Leader is the escalation layer above the individual SA for the hardest architecture, security, or compliance objections — brought in on RFPs, security questionnaires, and competitive deals that could stall without senior technical input, without replacing the SA as the deal's primary technical contact.
Commercial Technical Alignment (oversight)
The SA Leader ensures the team consistently connects technical requirements to commercial outcomes across the pipeline, and personally engages on pricing/packaging justification and expansion-signal strategy for the largest deals.
Internal Collaboration
Sales (Account Executives)
The SA Leader partners with Sales leadership to make sure SA/AE pairing is working at the portfolio level — owning the technical narrative in aggregate while sales leadership owns the commercial motion — and personally steps in when a specific SA/AE partnership needs adjudicating.
Partnerships
The SA Leader works with Partner Leads across every channel (Hyperscalers, Accelerators, SfP+OAuth, Solution Providers) to make sure SA support scales with each channel's motion, while commercial terms and channel strategy stay owned by the Partner Lead.
Engineering and Product
The SA Leader represents the aggregated market signal — patterns across deals, not just one opportunity — to engineering and product, and prioritizes which recurring technical blockers or roadmap gaps are costing the team deals versus which are one-offs.
Technical Account Management (TAM) and Customer Engineering
The SA Leader ensures handoff quality from pre-sale to post-sale is consistent across the team — auditing that architecture decisions, commitments, and open items are documented well enough that TAMs and CEs can drive early adoption without re-discovering the deal.
Success Metrics
SA Leader effectiveness is measured by commercial and technical outcomes across the whole team, not just their own deals:
Team ARR Bookings — new logo and expansion ARR across every SA's pipeline, relative to team quota
Deal Velocity — time from technical qualification to technical win, tracked across channels
PoC Win Rate — percentage of structured evaluations that convert to closed-won, team-wide
Pipeline Coverage — volume and quality of SA-engaged opportunities relative to quota, per channel
Handoff Quality — post-sale team satisfaction with documentation and deal context, across the team
Team health — ramp time to productivity for new SAs, retention of the SA team itself

Deine Capco Aufgaben
Du begleitest anspruchsvolle Transformations- und Technologieprojekte bei Banken, Versicherungen und weiteren Finanzdienstleistern und entwickelst gemeinsam mit unseren Kunden zukunftsfähige Lösungsarchitekturen.
Du berätst unsere Kunden ganzheitlich zu Solution-, Application-, Data-, Integration- und Cloud-Architekturen und übersetzt fachliche Anforderungen in tragfähige technische Lösungen.
Du entwickelst technische Zielbilder, Lösungskonzepte und Transformations-Roadmaps und begleitest deren Umsetzung von der Konzeption bis zur Implementierung.
Du bewertest bestehende Systemlandschaften und identifizierst Optimierungs- und Modernisierungspotenziale hinsichtlich Architektur, Integration, Skalierbarkeit, Sicherheit und Wartbarkeit .
Du unterstützt bei technologischen Entscheidungen, beispielsweise hinsichtlich Cloud-Plattformen, Integrationsarchitekturen, APIs, Microservices, Datenarchitekturen und geeigneter Technologie-Stacks .
Du fungierst als Schnittstelle zwischen Business, IT, Entwicklung und weiteren Stakeholdern und stellst sicher, dass fachliche und technische Anforderungen in einer konsistenten Gesamtarchitektur zusammengeführt werden.
Du baust professionelle und vertrauensvolle Beziehungen zu relevanten Stakeholdern unserer Kunden auf und vertrittst Architekturentscheidungen gegenüber technischen und fachlichen Ansprechpartnern.
Abhängig von Deiner Erfahrung übernimmst Du Verantwortung für Architektur-Workstreams, Teilprojekte und technische Teams und begleitest die Umsetzung der definierten Lösungen.
Neben der Projektarbeit bringst Du Dich in interne Themen ein, entwickelst unsere Technology- und Architecture-Capabilities weiter und teilst Deine Erfahrungen innerhalb von Capco.
Dein Capco Profil
Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium, beispielsweise in (Wirtschafts-)Informatik, Ingenieur- oder Naturwissenschaften , oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation sowie mehrjährige relevante Berufserfahrung.
Du verfügst über fundierte Erfahrung in der Konzeption und Umsetzung von Lösungsarchitekturen , idealerweise im Umfeld von Banken, Versicherungen oder anderen Finanzdienstleistern.
Du besitzt ein breites technologisches Verständnis und kannst komplexe fachliche Anforderungen in technische Architekturen und umsetzbare Lösungskonzepte überführen.
Du hast Erfahrung mit modernen sowie klassischen Systemlandschaften und kennst relevante Architekturprinzipien und -patterns, beispielsweise in den Bereichen Cloud, APIs, Microservices, Integration und Data .
Du verfügst über Erfahrung mit mindestens einer relevanten Cloud-Plattform und hast ein gutes Verständnis von Cloud-native Architecture, Security, Governance und Scalability.
Kenntnisse gängiger Programmiersprachen, Frameworks und Entwicklungspraktiken ermöglichen es Dir, Architekturentscheidungen auch auf technischer Ebene zu bewerten. Hands-on-Entwicklungserfahrung ist von Vorteil, aber kein zwingender Schwerpunkt der Rolle.
Du kannst unterschiedliche Lösungsoptionen hinsichtlich Business Value, technischer Machbarkeit, Kosten, Risiken und strategischer Zielarchitektur bewerten und entsprechende Empfehlungen ableiten.
Du bringst idealerweise Erfahrung in der Koordination technischer Teams und Workstreams sowie im Management unterschiedlicher fachlicher und technischer Stakeholder mit.
Ausgeprägte analytische und konzeptionelle Fähigkeiten, Kommunikationsstärke sowie ein hohes Maß an Eigeninitiative zeichnen Dich aus.
Fließende Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse sowie Flexibilität hinsichtlich hybrider Zusammenarbeit und Einsätzen vor Ort beim Kunden runden Dein Profil ab.

The AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact.

We work with customers across industries and digital-native businesses to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption.

The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and specialist delivery teams.
Within Education, we partner with universities, schools, research institutions, and countrywide education systems to advance responsible, mission-aligned uses of AI. These environments require more than technical deployment: success depends on institutional trust, thoughtful governance, stakeholder education, change management, and a value narrative that resonates with academic leaders, researchers, IT teams, faculty, administrators, and students.
This role is based in London. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance.

As an Applied AI Architect for Education, you will be the senior technical owner for a named portfolio of education customers and the primary technical counterpart to their leadership teams. You will act as the “CTO of your book of business,” shaping each institution’s AI strategy and guiding its journey from pre-sales discovery and solution evaluation through deployment, adoption, and measurable institutional impact.
You will own the technical account plan across ChatGPT Edu, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions. In partnership with the Account Director, you will translate institutional priorities into a focused portfolio of use cases, an actionable adoption roadmap, and a clear path to durable value and growth. The Account Director owns the commercial strategy; you own the technical strategy, customer journey, and path to production value.
You will work across academic, research, administrative, and operational contexts—helping customers determine where AI can responsibly improve teaching and learning, accelerate research, strengthen student and faculty services, and make institutional operations more effective.

You will account for the realities of education environments, including shared governance, complex stakeholder networks, academic calendars, accessibility, data privacy, responsible-AI expectations, and the need to build confidence among communities with differing levels of AI readiness.
You will remain accountable for the technical outcome while bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, enablement, security, product, education programs, and partners. This role calls for strong education-sector fluency, sound architectural judgment, and the ability to move confidently between executive strategy, academic and operational workflows, and hands-on technical conversations.

Serve as the primary technical advisor and long-term technical relationship owner for a named portfolio of existing education customers and pre-sales prospects.
Partner with Account Directors on account strategy while owning the technical account plan, technical milestones, adoption priorities, value-realization path, and expansion opportunities.
Lead discovery with institutional executives, academic leaders, researchers, faculty, administrators, and technical teams to identify and prioritize use cases connected to meaningful institutional objectives.
Translate education priorities into clear Applied AI Architectures spanning models, applications, institutional data, identity, integrations, security, privacy, governance, evaluation, and deployment.
Guide institutions through technical evaluations, demonstrations, workshops, prototypes, and proofs of value, building confidence in both the solution and its responsible path to production.
Translate institutional objectives into actionable adoption roadmaps with clear workstreams, sequencing, milestones, stakeholder ownership, governance, risks, success measures, and change-management needs.
Develop a focused use-case portfolio across areas such as teaching and learning, research, student and faculty services, knowledge management, software development, and administrative operations.
Translate institutional objectives into actionable adoption roadmaps with clear workstreams, sequencing, milestones, stakeholder ownership, governance, risks, success measures, and change-management needs.
Build trusted relationships and technical champions across CIOs, CTOs, CISOs, provosts, deans, research leaders, faculty, administrators, and other institutional stakeholders.
Qualify and coordinate support from Deployment Engineering, implementation, training and enablement, Product, Research, education specialists, partners, and other delivery teams.
Remain accountable for technical progress and customer outcomes while ensuring delivery teams own implementation execution once engaged.
Track adoption, usage, account health, production readiness, and measurable customer impact, intervening early when risks threaten value realization.
Identify repeatable education patterns and reusable architectures that can accelerate responsible adoption across institutions, departments, campuses, and education systems.
Translate field insights into actionable feedback for Product, Engineering, and Research, representing the needs and production patterns of education customers.
Help identify expansion opportunities where OpenAI can support additional academic, research, administrative, or operational workflows.

Deepening both your sales and technical skills through self driven education while taking advantage of all the professional development opportunities provided by Elastic.

A track record of success in a technical presales role within enterprise accounts -- enough experience selling and implementing technology to earn your customer’s trust.
A demonstrable ability to articulate and sell the benefits of modern platforms, software and technologies.
A real passion for being curious and a continuous learner. You are someone that invests in yourself as much as you invest in your professional relationships.

Testlio's fully managed crowdsourced testing platform, powered by our proprietary intelligence technology - LeoCore™, integrates expert, on-demand testers directly into your release process. Ship faster and more confidently with global coverage across 600,000+ devices, 800+ payment methods, 150+ countries, and 100+ languages. To learn more, visit testlio.com .
An exciting growth frontier for Testlio is digital payments and financial transactions. We are hiring a visionary and hands-on Payments Solutions Architect to lead the intersection of digital financial transactions and quality engineering. This role brings together deep practitioner expertise and strategic business leadership.

You will define, package, and oversee the quality of our payments testing offerings—establishing the catalog, methodology, staffing, and pricing—while diving deep into the technical architecture of complex transaction systems to solve quality engineering roadblocks.

You will imagine and drive innovative strategies to expand our payments business while delivering exceptional, hands-on value across our client portfolio.
Why you will love this job?
Blend Strategy with Technical Depth: Drive the overarching vision and commercial packaging of our Payments offerings while staying grounded in the technical architecture and delivery methodologies.
Shape the future of Payments Testing: Be at the forefront of innovation, building and evangelizing solutions that drive transaction integrity and quality across enterprise-level, global clients. Speak at conferences, author papers, collaborate with partners.
Partner with clients to solve complex challenges: Work directly with clients on deep technical integrations and architectural setups to shape testing strategies that deliver measurable value.
Make a tangible impact: Your work directly influences the success of our clients and the quality of their digital products. See your contributions translated into real-world improvements that benefit millions of users.
Drive company influence: Help build the pipeline, join sales calls and guide delivery on Payments opportunities, bringing your expertise to high-impact business decisions.
Why you will love being a part of Testlio?
Great Culture : Testlio is a female-founded company, and half of our team identifies as women. We’re proud of our inclusive, purpose-driven culture where people genuinely enjoy collaborating. As part of our team (we call ourselves TestLions), you’ll help create exceptional digital experiences for our customers, while also contributing to our freelance network.
Remote Work : Our culture is built around remote work. We’ve created systems to allow us to successfully work together asynchronously as a fully remote and globally distributed team . Testlio provides the tools and guidance for everyone to succeed in their careers in a fully remote setting. Our working style encourages everyone to make decisions, communicate effectively, and work at a sustainable pace.
Investment in You : Your growth and well-being matter to us. You’ll have flexible paid time off—including national holidays, personal days, and sick days—plus stock options so you can grow with Testlio. We also provide a $300 annual learning stipend to support your personal and professional development.
Winning Business : Testlio is growing, profitable, and cash-strong. We are leading our industry with exceptional clients who provide us with a high NPS score and a 4.7 rating on G2. Our business model is global, enterprise, and subscription-based. Several of our largest clients have been with us for 7+ years, and many spend $500K+/year with Testlio.

Vision Activation & Marketing: Imagine, drive, evangelize, and activate a viewpoint on the future of Payments Testing. Produce white papers, articles, posts, speeches, and webinars.
Ecosystem & Alliances Support: Collaborate with the Testlio VP, Alliances and external software partners to identify and execute joint GTM offerings with payments and commerce consultancies.
Sales Collaboration: Engage with enterprise-class prospects in partnership with Testlio Sales. Provide authentic and clear guidance on effective Payments Testing strategies, tactics, and ROI.
Offering Lifecycle Management: Launch, evolve, and refine payments services, based on market and competitive intelligence.
Collaboration on Hands-on Delivery
Architectural Design: Dive deep into client digital transaction architectures to design bespoke, highly technical quality engineering methodologies for agentic payments, mobile payments, wallets, and POS systems.
Delivery Expertise: Act as an escalation point and subject-matter expert for Delivery, stepping in hands-on from scoping to test execution review on complex or strategic payments engagements.
Technical Problem Solving: Solve technical roadblocks in payments quality engineering, ensuring transaction integrity, security, and compliance across different global regions and instruments.
Client Up-Leveling: Dive into intellectually stimulating, and 100M+ user scale-impacting work. Help Testlio Services teams and top clients see, design, and implement new technical approaches.
What do you need to succeed?
Technical Skills
Deep Payments Experience: 10+ years of deep experience with digital payment systems, including mobile payments, online banking, payment gateways, wallets, and point-of-sale systems.
Quality Engineering Affinity: Strong technical affinity for quality engineering, API integrations, and world-class software development methodologies within the financial sector.
Hands-on Troubleshooting: Demonstrated ability to dive into the technical architecture, troubleshoot payment integrations, and design structured evaluation criteria for complex transaction flows.
Education: Master's degree in Finance, Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field preferred.
Human Skills
Proven Client-Facing Experience: Strong management consulting or managed services background with a client-centric mindset and ability to lead technical discovery.
Commercial & Strategic Acumen: Experience designing service offerings, understanding cost-to-serve dynamics, and collaborating cross-functionally across sales and partners.
Systems Thinker: Keen intellect, vivid imagination, and rapid problem-solving capabilities, paired with a "lifetime learner" approach to functional application.
Communication: Excellent written, visual, and oral communication capabilities enabling clear message delivery and active listening to both technical teams and business executives.
Leadership: Strong leadership ability to motivate and inspire distributed cross-functional teams without direct people management burden.
What is the application process?
At Testlio, we aim to hire individuals who are excited about their role, thrive in a fully remote environment, and have strong long-term potential with our team. Because we are a fully distributed company, our interview process includes conversations with several team members so you can get a well-rounded understanding of the role, the people you’ll work with, and how we collaborate. As a result, our interview process typically takes 3–4 weeks to complete.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Agentic AI Architect-Anthropic based in United Kingdom.
As an Agentic AI Architect, you will shape and deliver enterprise-grade AI solutions that combine generative AI, machine learning, data, cloud technologies, and intelligent automation.

You will design scalable architectures that connect Claude and other AI technologies with enterprise knowledge, applications, APIs, workflows, and mission-critical systems. The role offers significant technical ownership, from discovery and architecture through deployment, evaluation, governance, and optimization.

You will work closely with client stakeholders, consultants, data engineers, AI/ML specialists, and platform teams to turn complex business needs into practical solutions. A strong focus will be placed on agentic workflows, RAG, tool use, structured outputs, responsible AI, and human oversight.

This is an opportunity to work at the forefront of enterprise AI while helping organizations adopt powerful technologies securely and responsibly. Travel to clients and conferences may be required as needed.
Accountabilities
Architect, develop, deploy, and maintain scalable AI, machine learning, generative AI, and agentic AI solutions for enterprise use cases.
Define end-to-end architectures covering data ingestion and preparation, model selection, orchestration, APIs, integrations, user experiences, monitoring, security, and governance.
Partner with business and technical stakeholders to identify high-value AI opportunities, translate requirements into technical designs, and establish delivery roadmaps.
Lead technical discovery sessions, architecture workshops, design reviews, proof-of-concepts, demonstrations, and solution delivery activities.
Design and implement LLM-powered applications using Claude, Anthropic APIs, and other appropriate LLM platforms.
Apply prompt and context engineering techniques, including instruction design, few-shot examples, structured inputs and outputs, response constraints, and long-context management.
Architect secure RAG solutions using enterprise documents, knowledge bases, databases, and other approved information sources, including ingestion, chunking, embeddings, retrieval, reranking, citations, and response generation.
Build agentic systems capable of reasoning over enterprise context, using authorized tools, executing multi-step tasks, and coordinating workflows across enterprise applications.
Define agent roles, task boundaries, permissions, memory and context strategies, approval gates, fallback mechanisms, and escalation paths.

The Senior Director, Platform Architecture owns the end-to-end technical architecture for the Agentic Service Catalog. You are responsible for ensuring that the platform operates as one secure, scalable, governable, and maintainable system even though its capabilities, data, workflows, integrations, and AI services are supplied by many teams.
You will define the contracts that make the federated model work: APIs, workflows, events, schemas, integration boundaries, identity, policy, approvals, evidence, observability, versioning, compatibility, and ownership boundaries.
This is a hands-on engaged manager architecture role, not an architecture-review-only position. This job reports to the Vice President Intelligent Automation and Data Platforms
Target-State Architecture
Manage and evolve the target-state architecture for the Agentic Service Catalog and its supporting workflow, control, and knowledge capabilities.
Establish how the platform integrates with service management, source control, CI/CD, cloud, observability, security, network, data platforms, identity, and other enterprise systems.
Ensure enterprise systems remain while the Service Catalog assembles usable context and governed workflows around them.
API, Workflow, Event & Data Contracts
You will define standards for APIs, events, workflow interfaces, schemas, errors, idempotency, retries, compensation, observability, versioning, and compatibility.
You will establish the technical contract for every reusable capability contributed to the Service Catalog.
Design stable interfaces that allow domain-owned capabilities to evolve without breaking user journeys or long-running workflows.
Ensure critical interfaces are typed, versioned, testable, observable, and connected to a named owner and support model.
Governance & Control-Plane Architecture
Design runtime policy gates for sensitive and production-affecting activities and ensure side effects occur only through governed execution paths.
Ensure actions are attributable to an authenticated principal, registered capability, policy decision, approval state, execution record, and evidence package.
AI & Agent Architecture
Establish clear separation between AI reasoning and durable workflow execution so model behavior never becomes the accidental source of execution truth.
Ensure AI agents work with enterprise systems through registered, typed, policy-aware service interfaces rather than direct database access or broad credentials.
Establish patterns for tool access, grounded context, retrieval, memory, policy enforcement, evaluation, evidence capture, human approval, replay, operational monitoring, and kill switches.
Hands-On Engineering & Reference Implementation
Build reference implementations that demonstrate approved patterns for capability registration, policy enforcement, workflow execution, evidence generation, enterprise integration, and AI/tool invocation.
Perform technical spikes and proofs of concept for high-risk or uncertain architectural decisions.
Cross-Team Technical Leadership
Coordinate technical direction across Service Catalog engineering, delivery teams, domain capability providers, enterprise architecture, Security, Risk, AI Platform, ITSM, Cloud, Data, Network, and infrastructure teams.
Define what the central platform owns, what capability providers own, and what service teams continue to oversee.
Create architecture review and exception processes that protect the platform without becoming delivery bottlenecks.
Mentor engineers and architects and raise technical capability across contributing teams.
8+ years of experience in management
8+ years of experience with platform architecture
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or experience in lieu of education
Think end to end, connecting user-facing applications, APIs, workflows, integrations, data, security, governance, AI capabilities, infrastructure, and operational concerns into architecture.
Experience with API and integration design, including contracts, schemas, versioning, compatibility, error handling, and boundaries.
Practical experience with AI-enabled systems, agent architectures, model integration, intelligent automation, or related latest technologies.
You have experience with enterprise security and governance concepts including identity, authorization, least privilege, policy enforcement, approvals, auditability, evidence, and traceability.
Establish reusable technical standards and reference patterns that other engineering teams can implement.
You will be hands-on, including development, prototyping, code review, integration troubleshooting, and technical mentoring.

About Zelara
Most CRM marketing still blasts generic messages at scale and calls it "personalization." Our founders experienced this firsthand in senior roles at HelloFresh, Salesforce, Uber, and others. Backed by top-tier VCs, they decided to build a better way.
Zelara is an agentic lifecycle marketing platform that improves with every interaction. It works with the CRM infrastructure our customers already use, replacing static journeys and manual segmentation with a system that creates content, makes individual-level decisions, and learns from every outcome.
With bunq, Europe's second-largest neobank, we delivered +7.4% activation and +66% reactivation uplift , measured against a control group. We raised a €3M pre-seed and are generating revenue with paying enterprise customers. Now we are hiring our first Solutions Architect to make the path from integration to measurable value repeatable.

This is a deeply technical customer role centered on post-sales value realization, with involvement in pre-sales discovery. It is not conventional customer success built around reactive support and business reviews, nor a pre-sales role that hands off at signature.
You will own technical value realization for a portfolio of customers, from discovery and onboarding through live experiments, measured results, and scaled adoption.
You and the commercial lead run each account as a pair, in a weekly rhythm and in the room together for the conversations that decide something. They own pricing, proposals, contracts, conversion to an annual contract, expansion, and renewal. You own the technical plan and evidence behind those decisions.

Before signature, you lead technical discovery alongside them. After signature, you become the customer's named technical lead, accountable for solution design, data mapping, the experiment plan, stakeholder coordination, and go-live. You make value real and defensible; the commercial lead owns the close.
There is no separate customer success manager, and we are not planning one. The two of you hold the whole relationship: the commercial lead is the account owner, you are the technical owner, and the working relationship with the customer's CRM, data, and analytics teams is yours.
Your focus is the customer-specific application of Zelara's platform. Product owns the roadmap and prioritization. Engineering owns production software, reusable integrations, reliability, and security. Science owns the learning methods and models, experimental methodology, and causal measurement standards. You turn their work into a functioning customer solution and bring in each team when a requirement crosses those boundaries.
Today our founders lead the technical side of every customer relationship. You will take over that responsibility and build the function as the customer base grows.
You will work with mid-market and enterprise B2C companies across Europe: fintech, e-commerce, travel, and employee benefits. Successful pilots grow into long-term, scaled deployments.

Own the technical customer journey from discovery through onboarding, pilot delivery, measured value, and scaled adoption
Lead technical discovery before signature: understand how the customer makes money and which metric moves it, then validate the integration path, available data, measurement feasibility, and what the pilot can credibly promise
Own onboarding: align stakeholders, define the data mapping and acceptance criteria, coordinate implementation, and take the customer live on its existing CRM stack
Design and pre-register each customer experiment using Zelara's scientific standards: hypothesis, primary metric, cohort, control group, conversion window, success threshold, and decision rules, because a success bar set after seeing the data is not a result
Own the customer-facing interpretation of results: reconcile Zelara's analysis with the customer's data, involve Science in novel or ambiguous analyses, and state clearly when the evidence is not decision-ready
Enable the customer's team to operate campaigns independently rather than becoming the person who runs them
Partner with the commercial lead on annual contracts, expansion, and renewal: identify the opportunity, quantify the value, and de-risk the technical plan
Drive the product loop rather than report into it: turn recurring customer needs into product opportunities, engineering requirements, and research questions, and bring the evidence from live accounts that decides their priority
Build what closes the gap in the meantime: use agents to produce the scripts, tooling, and prototypes that unblock an account before the platform covers it
Your First 90 Days
30 Days (Immersion): Learn the platform and customer portfolio, join every active account, and take ownership of your first technical customer relationship.
60 Days (Ownership): Lead one onboarding independently, with the integration requirements, campaign configuration, experiment design, and measurement plan agreed before launch.
90 Days (Scale): Own a small portfolio, deliver your first evidence-backed results readout, use it with the commercial lead to inform an annual-contract or expansion decision, and improve the playbook based on live accounts.

You have led deployments, implementations, or technical accounts for mid-market or enterprise customers at a B2B SaaS company, and your work has influenced adoption, renewal, or expansion.
You judge a customer's business before you design for it: which metric their leadership is measured on, which one is decoration, and what matters that nobody has said out loud. You aim the solution at the first.
You can turn a business question into an analysis plan: define the right metric, cohort, and measurement window; identify what would disprove the claim; and judge whether the evidence is decision-ready.
You have led real customer integrations and know that a successful import is not the same as usable data.
You understand experiments: control groups, effect sizes, statistical power, conversion windows, and why the design has to be frozen before it runs.
You know the lifecycle marketing stack (Braze, Bird, Iterable, Klaviyo, Customer.io , Emarsys, HubSpot): what it does well, where it stops, and how a CRM team works inside it.
You are credible with a Head of CRM and their data engineer in the same hour, and you switch between them without losing either.
You say the uncomfortable thing early, and a commitment with a date on it is a commitment.
